items.title: How to Think Like the SQL Server and PostgreSQL Engines
items.author: Brent Ozar Unlimited
items.summary:
You’re a developer or a DBA, and you’re comfortable writing queries to get the data you need. You’re much less comfortable trying to design the right indexes for your database server. In my new totally free How to Think Like the Engines class, you’ll learn how the SQL Server and Postgres database engines look at your indexes and build your query results.

You’ll learn:

The differences between nonclustered indexes and clustered indexes (and why Postgres doesn't use clustered indexes at all)

Which kinds of indexes work better as a starting point for SQL Server, versus which ones work better for Postgres

The basics of execution plans on both platforms, and how to read them

items.title: AAIF Reading Group: Measuring Agent Policy Compliance
items.author: AAIF Live
items.summary:
Measuring Agent Policy Compliance: Are AI Agents Following Their Intended Policies?

How do we measure whether an AI agent is actually following its intended policies?

Join the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) community for an informal reading group exploring the paper “Measuring Agent Policy Compliance.”

Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25398

We’ll read through the paper together, unpacking its approach to measuring policy compliance in AI agents, examining its key ideas and assumptions, and discussing the challenges involved in evaluating agent behavior.

This is not a formal presentation or lecture. It’s a community conversation: bring your questions, interpretations, disagreements, and ideas. We’ll leave plenty of room for open discussion and constructive debate.

We’ll explore:

- How agent policy compliance can be measured
- The paper’s methodology and key ideas
- Challenges in evaluating whether agents follow their intended policies
- Assumptions and limitations of the proposed approach
- Questions and perspectives from the community
- What this could mean for building and evaluating more reliable AI agents

If you’ve read the paper already, come ready to share your perspective. If you haven’t, you’re still welcome - we’ll work through it together.

Come curious. Bring questions. Let’s read the paper together and see where the discussion takes us.

## About the Agentic AI Foundation

The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) is the open, neutral home for the agentic AI ecosystem, bringing together developers, researchers, companies, and communities to build open standards and infrastructure for interoperable AI agents.

Learn more: Agentic AI Foundation

items.title: Bridging the Gap Between AI Builders and Domain Experts
items.author: AAIF Live
items.summary:
Everyone is racing to build one agent that can do everything. Justin Schroeder, co-founder of Standard Agents, thinks the future looks more like thousands of tiny ones. Ahead of his talk on domain-specific agents at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America, he explains why tightly scoped agents might be the smarter bet, even if it feels like a step back toward the single-purpose machine learning models of a few years ago.

We dig into standards as metadata you pin to an agent, so that it shows up with everything it needs in its harness. Then we test the idea against the obvious objection: if a big model can already handle the task, why scope down at all? The answer covers forcing functions, a microservices mindset for agent design, and small agents that quietly check issues or unread messages every five minutes. It also covers the surprise $1K bill waiting for anyone who leaves their agents running.

Then it turns into a proper debate. Our host is 99% sure the agent marketplace will never happen, and Justin arrives with a counter that might change his mind (hint: think about where your skills come from). Along the way, we cover agents as tools versus a big-brain router and how anyone keeps track of a thousand agents. We also talk about why the people who know what agents can do and the people who know what they need still have to meet in the middle.

Demetrios Brinkmann: https://www.linkedin.com/in/dpbrinkm
Justin Shroeder: https://www.linkedin.com/in/jpschroeder
